newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Saudi Aramco term naphtha talks in deadlock.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Aramco term naphtha talks in deadlock.

text.p: Talks between Saudi Aramco and its customers remain deadlocked with buyers unwilling to pay the $15 per tonne premium for the kingdom's full-range naphtha for sale on a six-month term basis, industry sources said on Friday.

Most Japanese term buyers who had initially hoped that Saudi Aramco would stick to the price set in the previous contracts, have raised their bids to $10-$12 per tonne premium to Aramco's full-range naphtha quotes.
In the previous contracts for January to June 1997, Saudi Aramco sold its full-range naphtha from Jubail at a $5.50-per-tonne premium, and from Rabigh at a $5.80-per-tonne premium.
Aramco sold its A-180 paraffinic naphtha at a $6.50-per-tonne premium.
Most of Saudi Aramco's 13 potential buyers said they hope that the company would consider lowering its offer prices.
For the sale of its A-180 term naphtha, Saudi Aramco has revised its target offer to a $17.00-premium, at the lower end of its earlier-set range of $17.00-$17.50.

While buyers were unwilling to pay the $15-per-tonne premium for the full-range naphtha, most seemed ready to accept the $17.00-per-tonne premium which Aramco is targetting for the A-180 paraffinic naphtha.
Traders said Saudi Aramco has also requested buyers to take on a package deal, lifting a combination of full-range and A-180 paraffinic naphtha.
But some buyers who would rather lift only one naphtha grade, traders said.
"It's tough to take both paraffinic naphtha and full range naphtha when some buyers prefer to take just one product," said a buyer familiar with the term talks.
Under the term deal, Aramco is expected to offer up to 2.9 million tonnes of A-180 parafinic naphtha--800,000 tonnes for loading from Jubail and 500,000 tonnes from Rabigh.
The deal also involves 2.9 million tonnes of A-180 paraffinic naphtha. Both grades are for lifting between July and December 1997.
They said the term talks were unlikely to be concluded by this week as Saudi Aramco had originally planned.
Interested buyers were expected to give their responses to to Saudi Aramco. The talks started on Monday.
